accepted_baseline.statement: PSD-PAY-A402 is a candidate payment access protocol that is independent from INS/L1, DEL/L2, and AUP/L3 authorization scenarios.
The completed PSD source provides a Candidate inventory of shared A402 payload fields, without freezing their header placement, requiredness, or wire schema.
The completed PSD source defines six transaction states and their allowed transitions; transition triggers, timeouts, compensation, and product mappings remain undecided.
The completed PSD source defines A402 error categories and recovery directions; the standard wire error object, codes, and valid_next_actions remain undecided.
All three ACT-native A402 Header values use Base64URL-encoded UTF-8 JSON with a protocol plus method envelope.
Payment-Validation is an optional seller response Header after proof validation; Product Profiles may map validation semantics without claiming the product emits that Header.

decisions.title: Canonical machine-contract source and versioning
decisions.owner_role: ACT Core spec owner / PSD DWG

options.summary: Protocol Buffers are authoritative; JSON Schema and language types are generated.
JSON Schema is authoritative for the HTTP-first candidate; language types are generated.
Normative prose remains authoritative and all machine contracts are illustrative.

decisions.title: HTTP header envelopes and encoding
decisions.owner_role: ACT Core spec owner / HTTP Binding owner / Product Profile maintainers

options.summary: All ACT-native A402 headers use Base64URL-encoded UTF-8 JSON with one shared envelope.
Core defines logical objects; each versioned Binding defines its encoding and envelope.
Each Product Profile defines encoding without an ACT HTTP interoperability contract.

decisions.title: method_id identity, version negotiation, and discovery

options.summary: method_id is a globally namespaced stable identifier; version is a separate field.
method_id embeds its version and changes whenever the method contract changes.
method_id remains Product Profile local and is not interoperable across profiles.

decisions.title: Original-request association, idempotency, and replay control
decisions.owner_role: HTTP Binding owner / PSD and Security DWG

options.summary: Require byte-identical replay of method, target, selected headers, and body.
Bind proof to a canonical request fingerprint and require idempotency controls for non-idempotent delivery.
Require only business-resource association and leave HTTP replay rules to Product Profiles.

decisions.title: Fulfillment confirmation and evidence boundary
decisions.owner_role: PSD and TSD DWG / Product Profile maintainers

options.summary: A successful Payment-Validation result also proves business fulfillment and closes the evidence lifecycle.
Payment validation, resource delivery, method-specific fulfillment confirmation, and TSD evidence remain distinct correlated facts.
Fulfillment and evidence are entirely Product Profile local after A402 validation and delivery.

decisions.title: Lifecycle, errors, and valid next actions

options.summary: Adopt the current six-state candidate transaction lifecycle as the complete Core lifecycle.
Define separate payment, validation, delivery, and fulfillment state machines.
Core preserves the six-state lifecycle as the public compatibility projection and adds structured phase outcomes and recovery actions; profiles map detailed states.

decisions.title: Confirmed commerce facts and cross-domain correlation

options.summary: Payment-Needed carries the minimum order and resource facts without referencing a separate CID confirmation object.
Payment-Needed carries payment identifiers and must reference a separately retrievable CID confirmation object.
The protocol fixes minimum order/resource correlation; a future CID rule may additionally embed or reference a separately confirmed object.

decisions.title: L1/L2/L3 publication and conformance scope
decisions.owner_role: ACT Core spec owner / ADD and PSD DWG

options.summary: Publish INS/L1, DEL/L2, and AUP/L3 together with equal conformance status.
Publish an INS/L1 prototype baseline; keep DEL/L2 and AUP/L3 validation-pending until ASL dependencies are public.
Do not publish any A402 candidate until all three authorization levels are complete.
Every Binding operation maps one-to-one to one Core message.
A workflow Binding may encapsulate multiple steps if it publishes coverage, inputs, observable outcomes, and evidence rules.
Workflow encapsulation is entirely Product Profile local and has no ACT coverage declaration.

deferred_pending_decisions.reason: The PSD-PMT-BND to Alipay wallet lifecycle mapping belongs to the PSD foundation and Alipay Product Profile, not the minimum A402 wire-contract packet.
AUP-specific machine error semantics belong to the AUP scenario specification; DP-A402-006 only defines the common A402 error envelope and recovery projection.
